why.text: A Vosges rain shadow gives a dry, sunny, semi-continental climate; hot days, cool nights and varied fault-line soils suit many aromatic grapes.

styles.text: Still wines, mostly white; reds and rosés come only from Pinot Noir, plus late-harvest and noble-rot sweet wines.

climate.text: Semi-continental: January averages 1.9 °C, July above 20 °C, with hot days and cool nights. Rain is 500 to 650 mm a year and sun about 1800 h a year at Colmar. The Vosges shield the vines from ocean influence.

soil.text: Very varied: shallow, acid-leaning brown soils on schist, granite or sandstone; sandy-gravelly alluvial soils; and calcareous brown or rendzina soils with marls and conglomerates.

altitude.text: Most vineyards lie between 200 m and 400 m, which the spec calls the optimal thermal belt.

tastes.text: Fresh, with natural tartaric acidity, intense aromas and good volume. Dry mineral wines, or softer fruity ones (Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris); they age well. Elegant Pinot Noir reds, plus light reds and rosés.

styles.name: Vendanges tardives
styles.text: Overripe hand-picked grapes, at least 18 months' ageing; exotic candied-fruit aromas, fresh finish.

styles.name: Sélection de grains nobles
styles.text: Overripe hand-picked grapes, at least 18 months' ageing; concentrated, long-lived, fruit-paste aromas.

styles.name: Edelzwicker
styles.text: Traditional blend of varieties; the label may not name any single grape.

styles.name: Clairet
styles.text: Fresh, fruity, light red or rosé from Pinot Noir; also called Schillerwein.

why.text: Hot days, cool nights and the Vosges screen give ripe grapes with natural acidity; lees ageing adds riper, often toasty notes.

styles.text: Traditional-method sparkling wine, white or rosé; rosé comes only from Pinot Noir.

climate.text: Semi-continental: cold winters (January mean 1.9 °C) and hot, dry summers (July above 20 °C). The Vosges shelter the vines; Colmar gets 1800 sunshine hours and the vineyards 500 to 650 mm of rain a year. Warm days and cool nights mark ripening.

soil.text: Very varied after the Rhine rift collapse: shallow acidic brown soils on schist, granite or sandstone; sandy-gravelly alluvial soils; and brown limestone or rendzina soils with marls.

altitude.text: Most vines grow between 200 and 400 metres.

tastes.text: Complex, naturally acidic, fresh and fine, with fruity notes. Lees ageing brings riper notes, often buttery or toasty. The mousse is fine and light.

styles.name: Brut
styles.text: The category in which the great majority of these wines are sold.

styles.name: Crémant d'Alsace
styles.text: Second fermentation in bottle, at least 12 months ageing from bottling.
